title: From question to answer: what happens inside an AI model

narration: Say Priya asks the company assistant one question.
When are expense claims due?
beats.visual_intent: Priya at her desk; the question types itself into a glowing chat panel in front of her.

grounding.claim: Priya and her question are an illustration

narration: Thirty days, it says.
She asks again. Sixty days.
Both sound completely sure.
beats.visual_intent: Striking open: two replies appear side by side under the same question, equally bright, contradicting each other.

grounding.claim: the two replies are an illustration of varying answers

narration: So which is right?
Follow her question inside the model.
beats.visual_intent: The camera pushes past the chat panel into the luminous space of the model, the question floating ahead.

grounding.claim: promise of the lesson

narration: First, her sentence breaks into small pieces.
Short words stay whole.
Longer ones can split in two.
beats.visual_intent: Striking moment: the typed question shatters into separate glowing pieces; one longer word visibly splits in two. Illustrative split, not a real tokenizer's output.

grounding.claim: text is split into tokens: whole common words, parts of longer words, punctuation
the exact split shown is illustrative

narration: Each piece is called a token.
Each token becomes a number.
Then a long row of numbers, learned in training.
beats.visual_intent: Each piece flips into a number tag, then unfolds into a long column of faint digits.

grounding.claim: each token maps to an ID from a fixed vocabulary
each ID becomes an embedding, a learned list of numbers

narration: The model works only from what is in front of it.
Her question, the chat, its own reply.
That space is the context window.
Her policy is not in it.
beats.visual_intent: A bounded frame of light holds three bands: the question, earlier chat, an empty reply line; outside its edge a dim policy document drifts, never entering.

grounding.claim: the model works only from the context window: prompt, conversation, reply being written; it has a limit
information not put in front of the model is not available beyond training
Priya's policy not being in the window is part of the illustration

beats.delivery: plain, slower on the last line

narration: Here is the tricky part.
For the next piece, it weighs every earlier token.
Say expense and due weigh the most.
beats.visual_intent: Lines of light run from each token to an empty next slot; their thickness varies, the lines from 'expense' and 'due' thickest. Weights illustrative.

grounding.claim: attention gives each earlier token a weight for the next token
which tokens weigh most here is illustrative

beats.delivery: slow and even; this is the slowdown

narration: That weighing is called attention.
Weighing, not understanding.
beats.visual_intent: The weight lines hold; the word attention settles above them, quiet.

grounding.claim: attention weights are calculated from the text and learned patterns; not a person deciding

beats.delivery: calm, firm on the last line

narration: Still no answer.
Just pieces, and how much each one matters.
beats.visual_intent: Pull back: the tokens and their weight lines float in the model's space; the reply line is still empty.

grounding.claim: the answer has not been generated yet at this point

narration: Now it scores every token it knows.
How likely is each one to come next?
beats.visual_intent: A ranked column of candidate first words rises beside the empty reply, bars of different lengths, no numbers. Candidates illustrative.

grounding.claim: the model produces a probability for every token in its vocabulary, a ranked list
the candidate words shown are illustrative

narration: One is picked and added.
Then it all runs again.
Pick, add, repeat, until an end token.
beats.visual_intent: The chosen word flies from the list into the reply line, the weights redraw, and the loop runs faster: the reply grows word by word until a small end marker closes it.

grounding.claim: one token is chosen, appended, and the process repeats with the longer text
generation stops at an end-of-text token or a length limit

narration: Here is where people slip.
It did not look anything up.
It wrote likely pieces, one by one.
beats.visual_intent: A faint search box appears and is struck through; the growing reply line stays lit as the real source of the answer.
beats.misconception: the assistant looks the answer up

grounding.claim: the model writes likely text rather than looking facts up
training rewards likely next tokens

narration: Now you.
Say at the number, thirty and sixty both rank high.
How did she get both?
beats.visual_intent: The reply stops at the number slot; the ranked list shows 30 and 60 near the top, close in length. Illustrative ranking.

grounding.claim: the ranking of the two numbers is part of the illustration
each step has a probability for each candidate token

beats.delivery: your-turn: set it up, ask, then silence

narration: The pick is drawn from the odds.
Like a weighted dice roll.
Say one run lands on thirty.
Another, on sixty.
beats.visual_intent: Striking moment: the same reply line forks at the number slot into two branches, one ending in 30 days, one in 60 days.

grounding.claim: the token is usually sampled from the probabilities rather than always the top one, so answers differ between tries
the two outcomes are part of the illustration

beats.delivery: a pause before the fork, then clear

narration: That is called sampling.
A temperature setting makes it steadier, or more varied.
beats.visual_intent: The two branches hold; a simple dial labelled temperature turns low and the branches draw closer, turns high and they spread.

grounding.claim: this choosing from probabilities is sampling
temperature: lower is more focused and repeatable, higher more varied

narration: So which is true?
It never saw her policy.
Both are just likely text, said with equal confidence.
beats.visual_intent: The two answers sit side by side, equally bright; neither is connected to any document.
beats.misconception: a confident answer is probably right

grounding.claim: a confident fluent tone is not evidence of correctness
the model works only from its context window
Priya's policy was not given to the model

narration: Training rewards likely text, not checked text.
A fluent answer that is false has a name.
A hallucination.
beats.visual_intent: One answer's glow stays steady while a faint crack runs through it; the word hallucination settles below.

grounding.claim: training rewards likely text and does not by itself check truth
fluent, confident false statements are called hallucination

narration: Its built-in knowledge stops at a training cutoff.
Anything newer, it has not seen.
beats.visual_intent: A line of light ends at a marked cutoff; later items sit beyond it, dim.

grounding.claim: built-in knowledge stops at a training cutoff; later information unknown unless put in front of it

narration: Now you. Two replies.
One sums up a policy she pasted in.
One gives a deadline from nothing.
Which do you check first?
beats.visual_intent: Two reply cards side by side, the first linked by a line to a document inside the window, the second floating unlinked.

grounding.claim: the two replies are an illustration

narration: The deadline. Nothing backed it.
And sounding sure proves nothing.
Still, glance at the summary too.
beats.visual_intent: The unlinked card gets the check-first mark; the linked card gets a lighter glance mark.

grounding.claim: confidence is not evidence of correctness
even with supplied text the model can misreport it
check important claims, more when stakes are higher

narration: So Priya pastes in the policy, and asks again.
Now it has something real to work from.
beats.visual_intent: Back at Priya's desk: the policy document slides into the chat panel; inside, its pieces join the context window and the weight lines reach them.

grounding.claim: clear, specific context with the relevant document gives the model better material
Priya's action is part of the illustration

narration: She checks the date against the page before sharing.
Give it the source.
Check what matters.
beats.visual_intent: Priya holds the reply next to the policy page, finds the matching line, then sends; the two rules rest on screen.

grounding.claim: check important claims such as dates and policy details against a reliable source before sharing
good context improves odds but does not guarantee correctness
